name: collaborative-filtering
description: Collaborative filtering computed live from a 6-user x 6-movie ratings table: Pearson similarity and user-based kNN, matrix factorization by ALS and SGD (every epoch stored), the zero-fill / truncated-SVD fit, a k x lambda capacity sweep, the invertible-map invariance of the factors, mu + b_u + b_i biases, fold-in of a new user, and implicit-feedback weighted ALS (Hu, Koren & Volinsky 2008).
honesty_note: THE DATA IS A DESIGNED TOY. Ratings are R = P* Q*^T from hand-chosen taste vectors on named axes (Action, Romance, Sci-fi), so the table is exactly rank 3 and recoverable from its 30 observed entries. The DESIGNED vectors are authored; the LEARNED ones are genuinely fitted by ALS / SGD from a seeded random start and come out on different, unlabelled axes. A lesson must not present the designed axes as something the algorithm discovers.

implementation.sliders: Functions read their inputs through _init({getSlider}); an absent slider falls back to the toy default, so every function works in any scene. The state is rebuilt only when a slider it read changes; expensive runs (ALS, SGD, zero-fill, sweep, implicit ALS) are memoised by exactly their inputs, so moving a rotation slider never retrains.
implementation.initialisation: P then Q, row-major, uniform(0,1) from mulberry32(cf_seed). The checker re-implements mulberry32 bit for bit.
implementation.als: One epoch = every p_u then every q_i, each a ridge solve over that row's observed cells; lambda is not scaled by the row count.
implementation.sgd: Observed cells in row-major order; both updates use pre-step values; the factor 2 of the gradient is absorbed into gamma.
implementation.zero_fill: ALS on the full matrix (hidden cells = 0) with lambda = 1e-9 for 200 epochs, which converges to the truncated SVD (Eckart-Young).
implementation.fold_in: Against the DESIGNED movie vectors Q*, so your vector is readable on named axes; ridge 0.1.
implementation.implicit: Preference p = [count > 0], confidence c = 1 + alpha * count, ALS over all 36 cells, lambda 0.1, 30 iterations.

verified_values.note: Asserted by scripts/check_collaborative_filtering_domain.py, which also compares every function against an independent NumPy implementation. If a change breaks one, the lesson's arithmetic is wrong, not the test.
verified_values.als_test_rmse: 2.684 at init, 0.140 after 10 epochs, 0.068 after 300 (k = 3, lambda = 0.01, seed 1)
verified_values.zero_fill_test_rmse: 2.7315; the hidden 5s come out as 0.77 and 0.60
verified_values.capacity: k = 3, lambda = 0: exact; k = 5, lambda = 0: test RMSE 12.27; k = 5, lambda = 0.01: 1.06
verified_values.knn: n = 2: test RMSE 1.614; Dan x Die Hard = 2.75 from Ava and Eli (truth 3)
verified_values.baseline: mu = 2.967; mu + b_u + b_i test RMSE 1.232
verified_values.invariance: learned P = P* A with max residual 0.011

functions.cfUser: cfUser(u) — user name: Ava, Ben, Cleo, Dan, Eli, Fay.
functions.cfMovie: cfMovie(i) — movie title: Die Hard, Notebook, Arrival, Mr&Mrs Smith, Matrix, Her.
functions.cfGenre: cfGenre(f) — name of designed taste axis f: Action, Romance, Sci-fi.
functions.cfR: cfR(u, i) — current rating r_ui from cf_R (observed or hidden).
functions.cfObs: cfObs(u, i) — 1 if (u, i) is in the training set Omega, 0 if hidden (cf_obs).
functions.cfNObs: cfNObs() — number of observed ratings |Omega| (30 by default).
functions.cfMu: cfMu() — global mean mu of the observed ratings.
functions.cfUserMean: cfUserMean(u) — mean of user u's observed ratings.
functions.cfCoRated: cfCoRated(u, v) — number of movies both users rated.
functions.cfSim: cfSim(u, v) — Pearson similarity over co-rated movies, each user centered on their own mean; 0 with fewer than 2 co-rated.
functions.cfKnn: cfKnn(u, i, n?) — user-based kNN prediction r_u_bar + sum w (r_vi - r_v_bar) / sum |w| over the n most similar users who rated i (n defaults to cf_knn).
functions.cfKnnNbr: cfKnnNbr(u, i, rank, n?) — index of the rank-th neighbour cfKnn used, or -1.
functions.cfKnnRmse: cfKnnRmse(n?) — kNN test RMSE over the hidden cells.
functions.cfPstar: cfPstar(u, f) — designed taste of user u on axis f (cf_pstar overrides).
functions.cfQstar: cfQstar(i, f) — designed vector of movie i on axis f (cf_qstar overrides).
functions.cfStarPred: cfStarPred(u, i) — designed prediction q*_i . p*_u.
functions.cfQstarLen: cfQstarLen(i) — |q*_i|: 2 for a single-genre movie, 2.83 for a two-genre one.
functions.cfStarCos: cfStarCos(u, i) — cosine of the angle between p*_u and q*_i.
functions.cfP: cfP(u, f) — learned user factor at epoch cf_epoch for algorithm cf_algo (0 ALS, 1 SGD); 0 for f >= k.
functions.cfQ: cfQ(i, f) — learned movie factor, as cfP.
functions.cfPred: cfPred(u, i) — learned prediction q_i . p_u at the current epoch.
functions.cfPredAt: cfPredAt(u, i, e, algo?) — learned prediction at epoch e.
functions.cfTrainRmse: cfTrainRmse(e) — training RMSE at epoch e for the current algorithm.
functions.cfTestRmse: cfTestRmse(e) — test RMSE (hidden cells) at epoch e for the current algorithm.
functions.cfAlsTrain: cfAlsTrain(e) — ALS training RMSE at epoch e.
functions.cfAlsTest: cfAlsTest(e) — ALS test RMSE at epoch e.
functions.cfSgdTrain: cfSgdTrain(e) — SGD training RMSE at epoch e.
functions.cfSgdTest: cfSgdTest(e) — SGD test RMSE at epoch e.
functions.cfLoss: cfLoss(e) — the regularised objective sum_Omega (r - q.p)^2 + lambda(sum |p|^2 + sum |q|^2) at epoch e.
functions.cfZeroPred: cfZeroPred(u, i) — rank-k fit of the table with hidden cells set to 0 (= truncated SVD of the zero-filled matrix).
functions.cfZeroRmse: cfZeroRmse() — test RMSE of the zero-fill fit.
functions.cfSweepTrain: cfSweepTrain(k, lam) — ALS training RMSE with k factors and penalty lam (200 epochs).
functions.cfSweepTest: cfSweepTest(k, lam) — ALS test RMSE with k factors and penalty lam (200 epochs).
functions.cfMapA: cfMapA(r, c) — entry of the invertible map A = diag(cf_stretch, 1, 1) R_axis(cf_theta).
functions.cfMapP: cfMapP(u, f) — learned p_u after the map: p_u A (k = 3).
functions.cfMapQ: cfMapQ(i, f) — learned q_i after the compensating map: q_i A^-T (k = 3).
functions.cfMapPred: cfMapPred(u, i) — (p_u A).(q_i A^-T); equal to cfPred(u, i) for every A.
functions.cfFitA: cfFitA(r, c) — entry of the least-squares map A with P* A ~ P (learned P, k = 3).
functions.cfFitResid: cfFitResid() — largest |P* A - P| entry for that fit (0.011 by default).
functions.cfBaseline: cfBaseline(u, i) — baseline prediction mu + b_u + b_i.
functions.cfBaselineRmse: cfBaselineRmse() — test RMSE of the baseline.
functions.cfMe: cfMe(f) — your taste vector on (Action, Romance, Sci-fi), solved from cf_me against the designed movie vectors with ridge 0.1.
functions.cfMeR: cfMeR(i) — your rating of movie i from cf_me (0 = not seen).
functions.cfMePred: cfMePred(i) — your predicted rating of movie i.
functions.cfMeRated: cfMeRated() — how many movies you rated.
functions.cfMeTop: cfMeTop(rank) — index of your rank-th best unrated movie, or -1.
functions.cfPref: cfPref(u, i) — preference p_ui: 1 if watched at all, else 0.
functions.cfConf: cfConf(u, i) — confidence c_ui = 1 + alpha * count (alpha = cf_alpha).
functions.cfImpX: cfImpX(u, f) — implicit user factor from weighted ALS over ALL cells.
functions.cfImpPred: cfImpPred(u, i) — predicted preference x_u . y_i.
functions.cfImpPosOnly: cfImpPosOnly(u, i) — the control: a fit of the watched cells only, which predicts ~1 everywhere.
functions.cfImpTop: cfImpTop(u) — index of user u's top unwatched movie by predicted preference, or -1.

cf_R.description: Tensor [6,6], 1 to 5: the ratings table. Defaults to R = P* Q*^T. Editing a cell retrains everything downstream.

cf_obs.description: Tensor [6,6], 0/1: 1 = observed (training), 0 = hidden (test). Defaults to one hidden cell per row and column.

cf_knn.description: Neighborhood size n for cfKnn, 1 to 5.

cf_pstar.description: Tensor [6,3]: designed user tastes on (Action, Romance, Sci-fi).

cf_k.description: Number of latent factors k, 1 to 5.

cf_lambda.description: Regularization lambda for ALS and SGD.

cf_theta.description: Rotation angle in degrees for the invariance demo.

cf_stretch.description: Stretch of axis 0 applied before the rotation; the movie vectors get the inverse stretch.

cf_me.description: Tensor [1,6]: your ratings, 1 to 5; 0 = not rated.

cf_C.description: Tensor [6,6]: watch counts for implicit feedback. Default: a 5 was watched 6 times, a 4 twice, the rest never; Ava watched Her once.

cf_alpha.description: Confidence slope alpha in c = 1 + alpha * count.

collaborative filtering.markdown: Predicting what a user will like from the ratings of **many** users — no content features needed. Neighborhood methods borrow from similar users or items; latent-factor methods embed users and items in a shared space where a rating is a dot product.
collaborative filtering.prompt: Explain collaborative filtering: what problem it solves, why it needs no item features, and the difference between neighborhood and latent-factor methods.

rating matrix.markdown: $R \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$, users by items, with $r_{ui}$ known only on a small observed set $\Omega$. The Netflix Prize matrix was about $1.2\%$ filled.
rating matrix.prompt: Explain the rating matrix in collaborative filtering and why its sparsity is the central difficulty.

observed set.markdown: $\Omega = \{(u,i) : r_{ui} \text{ is known}\}$. Matrix factorization fits only these entries; a missing rating is **unknown**, not zero.
observed set.prompt: Explain the observed set Omega and why matrix factorization sums its loss only over observed entries.

Pearson similarity.markdown: $w_{uv} = \dfrac{\sum_{i}(r_{ui}-\bar r_u)(r_{vi}-\bar r_v)}{\sqrt{\sum_i (r_{ui}-\bar r_u)^2}\sqrt{\sum_i (r_{vi}-\bar r_v)^2}}$ over co-rated items. Mean-centering removes each user's personal rating scale.
Pearson similarity.prompt: Explain Pearson similarity between users in collaborative filtering and why each user is centered on their own mean.

latent factor.markdown: A learned coordinate shared by users and items. A rating is predicted as $\hat r_{ui} = q_i^\top p_u$. The axes are not labeled genres: any invertible $A$ gives the same predictions via $(PA)(QA^{-\top})^\top = PQ^\top$.
latent factor.prompt: Explain latent factors in matrix factorization and why the learned axes are not genres.

matrix factorization.markdown: Approximate $R \approx PQ^\top$ with $P \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times k}$, $Q \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times k}$, fitted on $\Omega$ only with an $L_2$ penalty (Koren, Bell & Volinsky 2009).
matrix factorization.prompt: Explain matrix factorization for recommender systems: the model, the objective, and why it is low rank.

ALS.markdown: Fix $Q$ and every $p_u$ has a closed form, $p_u = (Q_{I_u}^\top Q_{I_u} + \lambda I)^{-1} Q_{I_u}^\top r_u$; then fix $P$ and solve for $Q$. Each half-step cannot increase the loss.
ALS.prompt: Explain alternating least squares for matrix factorization and derive the per-user update.

SGD.markdown: For each observed rating, $e = r_{ui} - q_i^\top p_u$, then $q_i \leftarrow q_i + \gamma(e\,p_u - \lambda q_i)$ and $p_u \leftarrow p_u + \gamma(e\,q_i - \lambda p_u)$. Popularized by Simon Funk in the Netflix Prize.
SGD.prompt: Explain stochastic gradient descent for matrix factorization and compare it with ALS.

regularization.markdown: The $\lambda(\lVert p_u\rVert^2 + \lVert q_i\rVert^2)$ term. With few ratings per user and many factors, the unregularized fit memorizes the training cells and extrapolates wildly to the hidden ones.
regularization.prompt: Explain why matrix factorization needs regularization and what happens without it.

cold start.markdown: A new user or item has too few ratings to pin down its $k$-dimensional vector: with fewer than $k$ ratings the least-squares system is underdetermined and only $\lambda$ keeps it finite.
cold start.prompt: Explain the cold-start problem in collaborative filtering and common remedies.

implicit feedback.markdown: Behavior such as views, clicks or plays instead of stars. There are no negative examples: an unwatched item may be disliked or just unseen. Hu, Koren & Volinsky (2008) model a binary preference with a confidence weight.
implicit feedback.prompt: Explain implicit feedback in recommender systems and why it needs a different model from explicit ratings.

confidence weight.markdown: $c_{ui} = 1 + \alpha\, r_{ui}$: how much the loss trusts preference $p_{ui}$. Every cell is fitted, unobserved ones as low-confidence zeros.
confidence weight.prompt: Explain the confidence weight c_ui = 1 + alpha r_ui in implicit-feedback matrix factorization.

RMSE.markdown: $\sqrt{\tfrac{1}{|T|}\sum_{(u,i)\in T}(r_{ui}-\hat r_{ui})^2}$ on a held-out set $T$. The Netflix Prize goal was a $10\%$ cut from Cinematch's $0.9525$ to $0.8572$.
RMSE.prompt: Explain RMSE as an evaluation metric for rating prediction and its role in the Netflix Prize.
